spec: Ruled 2026-10-04 (Andrew, DECISIONS.md 'combat is tested only when the engine changed ...' and 'the same for content and kingdom changes: each kind of change runs its own tests'): 'We only need to test that mechanics work and fights work when we've changed the engine.' / 'there are other things in the same category: content changes, kingdom changes.' Today every change pays for every package's tests, measured 2026-10-03/04: root tools/combine.mjs runs a fixed SUITES list on every merge-back whatever the worker brought - content 94 s, kingdom 115 s, the engine's whole suite 275 s, the viewer's whole gate 481 s, 16 minutes; tools/gate.mjs runs 'control battles unchanged' (40 s) on every landing (86 of the 87 gate runs for viewer, kingdom and art items since 2026-10-01); wrap wants the engine suite on a tree that is every file but .state/ (tools/gate-progress.mjs treeHash), so a line in DECISIONS.md makes the last pass stale; and a content change walks the whole chain (new pack, viewer re-dump and its whole gate, kingdom rebuild and its suite) before the merge-back runs all of it again. The rule to build: a package's tests run when that package's own code changed, and not otherwise. Engine code (src/ without the generated content pack, test/, the tools the tests run, package and compiler config) -> the engine suite and the control battles. Content (content/gen, settled.json, the pipeline scripts) -> content's suite and its linter. Viewer code -> the viewer's gate. Kingdom code -> kingdom's suite. A regenerated file - the engine's content pack, the viewer's generated dumps, a built page, kingdom's generated items - is not a change to the package that holds it and starts no suite. A document, a ruling, .state/ and a log line change nothing. An item's own tests always run. One definition of 'this package's code' per package, used by its gate, by wrap and by combine - never a copy; extend tools/code-stamp.mjs (Andrew, 2026-10-01: what the battles are made of, and 'none of them may force viewer or kingdom to rebuild') rather than add a second fingerprint. Each suite records the stamp it passed on, and a stamp that has a recorded pass is not run again - in a landing, at wrap, or in combine (so a suite that passed in the worker's copy on the same code is not re-run by the merge-back). Everything together still runs once per chat, as ruled 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-30 ('the full suite runs once per chat'; 'fast by default; the full process kept'): combine --full runs all four suites as combine does today, and wrap refuses until a full run passed on the code being wrapped - so this folder is still only updated by a tree that was tested. That narrows 2026-10-01's 'runs the full tests on the combined game' to once per chat. Two things to keep true: (1) the control-battle golden - a new content pack can move the control battles, so shipping a pack re-records .state/baseline.hash (40 s) and says whether the fights moved, without failing the content item; otherwise the next engine item fails on a difference it did not make. (2) a skipped suite is printed and logged as skipped with its reason (.state/gauntlet-log.jsonl, combine's summary) - never as passed (Law 9). Tests, each seen red first: a tree that differs from the last pass only in a document or .state/ runs nothing and satisfies wrap's check; a one-character change under engine src/core runs the engine suite and the control battles; a pack-only change runs content's suite, re-records the golden and does not start the engine suite, the viewer's gate or kingdom's suite; a kingdom-only change runs kingdom's suite alone; a viewer-only change runs the viewer's gate alone; combine with a worker that brought only kingdom code runs kingdom's suite alone and prints the three it skipped and why; combine --full runs all four; wrap refuses without a full run. Then make the documents say it: engine/CLAUDE.md 'The Iron Gauntlet', viewer/CLAUDE.md and kingdom/CLAUDE.md where they describe their gates, the header of root tools/combine.mjs. Tooling ambiguities go in GBH SWITCHES.md (DISPLAY-RULES 18); GBH SWITCHES tests.followWhatChanged holds the defaults chosen at filing.
expect: A visual, kingdom or content change runs only its own package's tests at landing and at merge-back, and says which suites it skipped and why; an engine code change runs the engine suite and the control battles as before; a ruling written into DECISIONS.md makes no suite stale; a suite that passed on the same code is not run twice; all four suites still run together once per chat before the wrap (combine --full), so the shared folder is only updated by a tested tree; no skipped suite is recorded as passed; the control-battle golden is still true after a content change.

THE SPLIT SWING is the hard part and the reason the naive one-event-one-beat mapping is wrong: a projectile takes ~700ms, so the travel half plays on attack.declared/attack.hit and the impact half is HELD until damage.applied — otherwise the bolt lands on a target that already took the damage. attack.hit is DUR 0 on purpose: its beat is a Promise that resolves when the projectile lands, and the pump awaits that, not a number. The speed multiplier scales durations uniformly and must never scale ORDER — at x4 the split swing must still split.
